subtype: Honouring a colleague who pays the price [Observer]
passage:
Indu: Heard about the Kochi hospital deal. Are you okay?
Nirmala: They signed with the other vendor. I wouldn't promise go-live by March.
Nirmala: We both know it's June at best.
Indu: You were right to say June.
Nirmala: Tell that to my target sheet. Feels like I'm the only one who thinks it mattered.
Indu: You're not. At stand-up I told the team exactly why we lost it.
Indu: Pooja said she'd have been the one fixing a broken launch in April.
Indu: And I've asked our lead to write the reason in your quarterly notes, not just the loss.
Nirmala: ...thanks. I nearly said March, you know. For about five seconds.
Indu: Five seconds is human. What you actually said is what counts 🤍
Nirmala: Chai at 4?
Indu: Already saved the corner table.

qa.q: Which go-live month did Nirmala refuse to promise?
qa.a: Nirmala wouldn't promise go-live by March, because it's June at best.

qa.q: How can you tell that Indu is worried about Nirmala?
qa.a: Indu feels concerned and protective; Indu messages first with "Are you okay?" and has already spoken up for Nirmala at stand-up.

qa.q: Which of Indu's steps would help most at review time, and why?
qa.a: Asking their lead to write the reason in the quarterly notes, so the record shows why the deal was lost and not just the loss.

qa.q: What is it like for Nirmala before and after hearing what Indu did?
qa.a: At first Nirmala feels alone, as if nobody else thought honesty mattered; after hearing about the team, Nirmala admits the five-second temptation and asks for chai 🙂

grounding: Shows a colleague noticing someone lose a deal for refusing to make a false promise, and backing them in front of the team so honesty is not carried alone.

subtype: Honouring a colleague who pays the price [Observer]
passage:
The notice was pinned beside the collection window of the dairy cooperative: the new supervisor would be Deshmukh, not Anand. Varun read it twice while milk cans clanged behind him.
Everyone at the centre knew why. Before the district inspection, the secretary had asked Anand to "round up" the fat readings. Anand had written the real numbers and signed.
Now Anand sat at the testing bench, eyes on the machine, answering in single words.
At lunch Varun carried two steel tumblers of tea to the bench. "The farmers trust your register more than any notice," he said.
That evening, when the society met under the neem tree, Varun stood up. "Bhimrao-kaka's payment was right to the paisa because of Anand's readings." Two farmers nodded. Old Bhimrao came over and pressed Anand's shoulder.
Anand said little, but he stayed after the meeting and laughed once.

qa.q: Who was named the new supervisor on the notice?
qa.a: The new supervisor would be Deshmukh, not Anand.

qa.q: What was Varun feeling when carrying tea to the testing bench?
qa.a: Varun felt uneasy about the unfair notice and protective of Anand, wanting Anand to know the farmers trust the register.

qa.q: What could others at the centre do so Anand doesn't stand alone?
qa.a: Like Varun, they could say openly that Anand's honest readings protect the farmers' payments, and keep backing real numbers at the next inspection.

qa.q: How is Anand affected by what Varun said at the meeting?
qa.a: Anand had been answering in single words, but after the meeting he stayed back and laughed once, looking less alone.

grounding: Shows a worker at a village dairy centre noticing someone lose a promotion for refusing to falsify readings, and speaking up so that person is not left alone.
